questions.question: What are the WCAG 2.1 levels and the POUR principles?
questions.title: WCAG 2.1 Levels (A, AA, AAA) & POUR Principles Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What are the WCAG 2.1 levels and the POUR principles?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust; Conformance levels A, AA, AAA; AA is the common legal target.

**Classic weak answer:** Aiming for AAA blindly — AAA may conflict with brand or impair UX; AA is the standard legal target (ADA, EN 301 549).

**Senior finish:** Mention WCAG 2.2 updates (2023), 2.5.5 target size, and that most SaaS products standardize on AA + selected AAA.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **WCAG 2.1 Levels (A, AA, AAA) & POUR Principles Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are the WCAG 2.1 levels and the POUR principles?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust; Conformance levels A, AA, AAA; AA is the common legal target**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Aiming for AAA blindly — AAA may conflict with brand or impair UX; AA is the standard legal target (ADA, EN 301 549)**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention WCAG 2.2 updates (2023), 2.5.5 target size, and that most SaaS products standardize on AA + selected AAA**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust; Conformance levels A, AA, AAA; AA is the common legal target
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).


| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Aiming for AAA blindly — AAA may conflict with brand or impair UX; AA is the standard legal target (ADA, EN 301 549) |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **aiming for AAA blindly — AAA may conflict with brand or impair UX; AA is the standard legal target (ADA, EN 301 549)** and what you do instead.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **POUR: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust; Conformance levels A, AA, AAA; AA is the common legal target** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Aiming for AAA blindly — AAA may conflict with brand or impair UX; AA is the standard legal target (ADA, EN 301 549)** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention WCAG 2.2 updates (2023), 2.5.5 target size, and that most SaaS products standardize on AA + selected AAA**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: How do you meet WCAG color contrast and focus-indicator requirements?
questions.title: WCAG Color Contrast & Focus Indicators — AA Requirements
questions.direct_answer:
How do you meet WCAG color contrast and focus-indicator requirements?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text, 3:1 for UI components; visible focus outline required for keyboard users.

**Classic weak answer:** Removing the default focus outline with outline:none without providing a visible replacement — keyboard users lose all context.

**Senior finish:** Recommend :focus-visible over :focus for focus-ring display only on keyboard navigation, and 4.5:1 contrast tools (axe, Chrome DevTools).

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Recommend :focus-visible over :focus for focus-ring display only on keyboard navigation, and 4.5:1 contrast tools (axe, Chrome DevTools)
